record.paper_title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows
record.original_question: Given an n-bit prime p, a generator g of the multiplicative group F*_p, an element a in F*_p, and a positive integer k, is there a positive integer x whose binary representation contains at most k ones such that a = g^x?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Bounded Hamming Weight Discrete Logarithm. Let p be a prime whose binary representation has n bits, let g be a generator of the multiplicative group F_p^* of the finite field with p elements, let a ∈ F_p^*, and let k be a positive integer (the parameter). The Hamming weight of a positive integer x is the number of 1's in its binary representation. Decide whether there exists a positive integer x of Hamming weight at most k such that a = g^x in F_p^*. The question is whether this parameterized decision problem (with parameter k) is fixed-parameter tractable, that is, whether it can be solved in time f(k) · poly(n) for some computable function f.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed as an open problem of Downey and Fellows. The problem is known to be in XP (at most (kn)^k candidates to try), and a related bounded-sum-of-digits variant has been shown to admit subexponential-in-k randomized algorithms (Sun–Yang 2004), but whether the binary Hamming-weight discrete logarithm over F_p^* admits a true FPT algorithm of the form f(k)·poly(n) appears to remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: On the Bounded Sum-of-Digits Discrete Logarithm Problem in Finite Fields
status_evidence.snippet: The bounded sum-of-digits discrete logarithm can be computed in random time involving a subexponential function of the digit-sum bound w.
status_evidence.claim: A related sum-of-digits variant has subexponential-in-parameter algorithms, but this does not settle FPT for the binary Hamming-weight version.

status_evidence.title: Computing Low-Weight Discrete Logarithms
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms for computing discrete logarithms whose exponent has low Hamming weight.
status_evidence.claim: Active cryptographic work on low-weight discrete logs, but no FPT result of f(k)·poly(n) form for the decision problem is established.
